docs.title: Per-move settings
docs.text:
Every move command takes these as keyword arguments. They apply to that one move:

robot.move_joints(90, -105, 165, 0, -30, 180, speed=20, profile="trapezoid")

A setting you leave out takes its default. The commands in the last column change a default for every move sent after them; a move's own setting still overrides it. Some settings matter only for some moves: a command's page says which have no effect on it.

Setting Values Default Default set by speed A percent of each joint's speed limit, above 0 and at most 100. 1 means 1 %, and 0.5 half a percent. 100 % set_joint_speed() accel A percent of each joint's acceleration limit, above 0 and at most 100. 100 % duration Seconds. none (the speed decides) profile One of the profiles below. "ruckig" set_profile() jerk A percent of the jerk limit, above 0 and at most 100. 100 % ramp_fraction More than 0, up to 0.5. 0.25 blend A percent, or millimetres, depending on blend_mode. 0 set_blending() blend_mode One of the modes below. "exact_velocity" blend_continuity One of the two curves below. "c1" ik_solver One of the solvers below. "pinocchio" set_ik_solver() singularity_strategy One of the strategies below. "stop" samples A whole number. automatic dry_run True or False. False

docs.title: speed
docs.text: Scales every joint's speed limit for this move. A value of 0 or less, above 100 or not a number is refused when the move is sent (BAD_OPTIONS). Moves along a Cartesian path (straight lines, arcs, circles and splines) run at no more than 20 % of the speed limit, whatever this says.

docs.title: accel
docs.text: Scales every joint's acceleration limit for this move. A value of 0 or less, above 100 or not a number is refused when the move is sent (BAD_OPTIONS). A lower value gives gentler starts and stops and a longer move. It scales the jerk limit with it.

docs.title: duration
docs.text: The move takes exactly this long, overriding speed. A duration of 0 or less fails with INVALID_DURATION; one shorter than the limits allow fails with DURATION_INFEASIBLE. A pause (delay()) takes it in place of its seconds.

docs.title: profile
docs.text:
How the move speeds up and slows down.

Value What it does "trapezoid" Limits speed and acceleration. Shorter moves; the arm can ring briefly after a full-speed stop. "quintic" A smooth polynomial shape that starts and ends at rest. "s_curve" A smooth fixed shape, with the gentlest jerk of the fixed shapes. "toppra" The fastest timing along the path within speed and acceleration limits. Needed for "zone" and "tolerance" blending. "ruckig" Limits speed, acceleration and jerk. Smooth starts and stops, with no ringing after a fast stop.

Also accepted: "poly5" for "quintic", "s-curve" for "s_curve", "scurve" for "s_curve", "smoothstep7" for "s_curve", "trap" for "trapezoid", "trapezoidal" for "trapezoid".

docs.title: jerk
docs.text: Only with profile="ruckig", the only profile that limits jerk: jerk=25 is four times gentler. A value outside 0 to 100 % is refused when the move is sent (BAD_OPTIONS); with any other profile the move fails with PLAN_FAIL.

docs.title: ramp_fraction
docs.text: Only with profile="trapezoid": the share of the move spent speeding up, and again slowing down. 0.5 leaves no constant-speed part. A value outside the range is refused when the move is sent (BAD_OPTIONS); with any other profile the move fails with PLAN_FAIL.

docs.title: blend
docs.text: How much of a corner is rounded or kept at speed. With "exact_velocity" it is the percent of the corner speed kept, 0 to 100 (0 stops at every waypoint). With "zone" it is the radius of the rounded corner, and with "tolerance" the largest distance from the path, both in millimetres.

docs.title: blend_mode
docs.text:
How a move joins the next one. "zone" and "tolerance" need profile="toppra", and "ruckig_corner" needs profile="ruckig" and joint moves. Without that, the moves are not refused: they run one by one, without blending, and the robot's log says so.

Value What it does "exact_velocity" Passes exactly through each waypoint, keeping part of its speed through it. "zone" Rounds each corner with a curve of radius blend. "tolerance" Rounds each corner so the path never strays more than blend from the programmed one. "ruckig_corner" Experimental. Jerk-limited corners, for joint moves only.

Also accepted: "g64" for "tolerance", "ruckig" for "ruckig_corner", "velocity" for "exact_velocity".

docs.title: blend_continuity
docs.text:
The shape of a rounded corner.

Value What it does "c1" The corner's direction changes smoothly, but its curvature jumps where it meets the straight path. "c2" The curvature also starts and ends at zero, so there is no jolt where the corner meets the path; the arm goes slower through the corner.

Also accepted: "quad" for "c1", "quadratic" for "c1", "quintic" for "c2".

docs.title: ik_solver
docs.text:
The solver that turns poses into joint angles. Joint moves do not use it.

Value What it does "pinocchio" Damped least squares on the Pinocchio model. "roboticstoolbox" Levenberg-Marquardt on the robotics toolbox model.

Also accepted: "pin" for "pinocchio", "robotics_toolbox" for "roboticstoolbox", "rtb" for "roboticstoolbox".

docs.title: singularity_strategy
docs.text:
What to do at a singular pose on a Cartesian path. Only "stop" is built; the robot refuses the other two when the move is sent (BAD_OPTIONS). Joint moves do not use it.

Value What it does "stop" Checks the whole path before the move starts and refuses a path through a singular pose. "variable_velocity" (refused for now) Reserved, not built yet. Would slow down through the singular region. "auto_avoid" (refused for now) Reserved, not built yet. Would bend the path around it.

Also accepted: "avoid" for "auto_avoid", "var_vel" for "variable_velocity".

docs.title: samples
docs.text: How many points a Cartesian path is planned and checked at: 2 to 500 for a straight line, 2 to 3000 for an arc, circle or spline; a value outside is clamped. Meant for planning tools. Joint moves do not use it.

docs.title: dry_run
docs.text: True plans the move in full and runs every check (joint limits, safety zones, self-collision, the timing) without moving the arm, on every move type.

docs.title: Not a per-move setting
docs.text: • completion_policy is refused on a single move (BAD_OPTIONS): use set_completion_policy() instead of a per-command option.

docs.title: Connection and events commands
docs.text:
The calls that connect a program to the robot, report the connection, and register functions the client calls when something happens.

  • connect() first. It checks that the robot speaks this client's protocol.
  • Callbacks run on the client's own receiving thread. Keep them short, and never wait for the robot inside one.
Command What it does Runs connect Connect to the robot and check its command protocol version. In the client disconnect Close the connection to the robot. In the client connected Whether the client is connected to the robot. In the client on_error Set a function to call when the robot sends an error event. In the client on_status_change Set a function to call each time the robot's status arrives. In the client on_motion_complete Set a function to call when a queued command of this client finishes. In the client on_motion_error Set a function to call when a queued command of this client fails. In the client remote_ip Return the robot's IP address on this connection. In the client local_ip Return this computer's IP address on the route to the robot. In the client local_label Return this connection's address as the robot names it. In the client

docs.title: Diagnostics and service commands
docs.text:
The service functions: a test move of one joint, a joint free to turn by hand, the Hall sensor check, the drives' gains, the control loop's read order, log levels, telemetry captures and recipes, and the motion filters.

  • For setting up and servicing a robot, not for production programs.
  • Some move a joint or take its torque away. Their pages say so in a warning.
Command What it does Runs joint_test Move one joint a few degrees and back, as a powered test. At once free_joint Free one joint so it can be turned by hand. At once hall_check Start or stop the Hall sensor check: its joint goes limp. At once set_pid_gains Set the control gains and limits of one joint's drive. At once set_can_read_first Choose whether the robot reads CAN first in each control tick. At once set_log_level Set the level of one of the robot's loggers, without a restart. At once capture_telemetry Record the robot's per-tick data into a file on the robot. At once stop_capture End the running telemetry capture now and save what it has. At once set_recipe Choose the telemetry recipe that the robot's data streams carry. At once reload_recipes Read the telemetry recipe files again and use them at once. At once reload_filters Read the signal filter file again and apply it at once. At once

docs.title: Gripper commands
docs.text:
The commands that open, close and move the gripper, wait for it, read how its last move ended, and set how it is driven.

  • Open, close and move are queued with the moves, in program order. The robot starts the jaws once it has sent the moves before them, so the jaws can move while the arm still moves.
  • The settings run at once. GripperResult is what gripper_result() returns.
Command What it does Runs GripperResult One gripper command's outcome: why its jaws stopped. In the client (a class) open_gripper Open the gripper's jaws fully, as a queued command. Queued close_gripper Close the gripper's jaws fully, as a queued command. Queued move_gripper Move the gripper's jaws to a position, as a queued command. Queued wait_gripper_move_complete Wait until this client's last gripper command has settled. In the client wait_holding_part Wait until the last gripper command has settled holding a part. In the client wait_released_part Wait until the last gripper command has settled with the jaws clear. In the client gripper_result Return the outcome of this client's last settled gripper command. In the client calibrate_gripper Calibrate the gripper: find both ends of its jaws' travel. At once set_gripper_ctrl_mode Switch the gripper between motor mode and firmware mode. At once set_gripper Give the gripper a target at once, outside the queue. At once

docs.title: I/O commands
docs.text:
The commands that switch the control box's isolated digital outputs and read its isolated digital inputs.

  • Pins 1 to 3 on each side. The robot reads and writes them every control cycle, in every mode.
  • An output keeps its level until a program changes it.
Command What it does Runs set_digital_output Switch one of the control box's isolated outputs on or off. At once get_digital_input Return whether one of the control box's isolated inputs is on. At once

docs.title: Jogging commands
docs.text:
The commands that move one joint at a time on request, as a teach pendant's jog buttons do, and the settings for how a jog speeds up and brakes.

  • JOG mode first: enter_jog_mode(). A joint moves while jog() asks for it and stops at jog_stop() or at a limit, where it brakes by itself.
  • Joints are counted from 0 in jog(): 0 is J1, 5 is J6.
Command What it does Runs jog Start jogging one joint: it moves until jog_stop() or a limit. At once jog_stop Stop jogging: the joint brakes to rest along its path. At once set_jog_accel Set the jog's ramp time, from rest to a joint's full speed. At once set_jog_profile Set the jog's profile: with its jerk limited, or not. At once set_jog_jerk_factor Set the jog's jerk, as a multiple of its acceleration. At once set_jog_control_mode Set how the drives follow a jog: PID or PD control. At once

docs.title: Motion commands
docs.text:
The moves a program queues: to joint angles or a pose, along straight lines, arcs, circles and smooth curves, and a timed pause between them.

All motion commands:

  • Are queued. A call returns once the robot has accepted the move, and the robot runs the moves in the order they were sent. Call robot.wait_idle() to wait until they have finished.
  • Need EXEC mode. Every move also needs the robot enabled and homed; a pause only needs EXEC mode.
  • Take per-move settings as keyword arguments, such as speed, profile or blend. They apply to that one move. Every setting is on the Per-move settings page.

Positions are in metres. Pose angles are in radians, or degrees with angle_unit="deg". Joint angles are in degrees.

Command What it does Runs move_joints Move every joint to a target angle, in joint space. Queued move_pose Move the tool to a pose, with the joints moving in joint space. Queued move_linear Move the tool in a straight line to a pose. Queued move_linear_rel_world Move the tool in a straight line by an offset along the base axes. Queued move_linear_rel_tool Move the tool in a straight line by an offset along its own axes. Queued move_arc Move the tool along a circular arc through a via pose to an end pose. Queued move_arc_rel_world Move the tool along a circular arc given by offsets along the base axes. Queued move_arc_rel_tool Move the tool along a circular arc given by offsets along its own axes. Queued move_circle Move the tool around a circle about a centre point. Queued move_circle_rel_world Move the tool around a circle given relative to the base axes. Queued move_circle_rel_tool Move the tool around a circle given relative to its own axes. Queued move_spline Move the tool along a smooth curve through a list of poses. Queued move_spline_rel_world Move the tool along a smooth curve through offsets along the base axes. Queued move_spline_rel_tool Move the tool along a smooth curve through offsets along its own axes. Queued delay Wait a given time between two queued moves. Queued

The relative moves end in _world or _tool, for the frame their offsets are measured in:

  • _world: along axes parallel to the robot's base frame.
  • _tool: along the tool's own axes, as they are when the move starts.

docs.title: Other names
docs.text:
Some commands have a second name from earlier versions of the library. Both names do exactly the same, in a program and in a raw protocol message, and programs that use the second name keep working. New programs use the names on these pages.

Other name Same as move_linear_rel_wrf move_linear_rel_world move_arc_rel_wrf move_arc_rel_world move_circle_rel_wrf move_circle_rel_world move_spline_rel_wrf move_spline_rel_world move_linear_rel_trf move_linear_rel_tool move_arc_rel_trf move_arc_rel_tool move_circle_rel_trf move_circle_rel_tool move_spline_rel_trf move_spline_rel_tool

docs.title: Motion settings commands
docs.text:
The settings every queued move uses unless the move passes its own: the speed, the motion profile, blending, the inverse kinematics engine, and when a move counts as complete.

All of them:

  • Set a default for this robot, not for one move. A move's own setting, passed as a keyword argument, wins for that move. Every setting is on the Per-move settings page.
  • Last until changed or until the robot software restarts, for every client.
Command What it does Runs set_joint_speed Set the default speed of queued moves, as a share of the limits. At once set_profile Set the default profile: how queued moves speed up and slow down. At once set_blending Set the default blend: how queued moves join at their corners. At once set_ik_solver Set the default IK solver, which turns poses into joint angles. At once set_completion_policy Set when the robot counts a queued move as finished. At once

docs.title: Real-time interface commands
docs.text:
The commands that let a PC stream joint targets to the robot itself, every control cycle or at a lower rate, and the settings of that stream. RTIClient is the client class that streams them.

  • The two contracts: hard real time, one target for every control cycle (4 ms) over UDP, each carrying its send time; soft real time, rti_connect(pc_ip, rate_hz=...), where the robot moves smoothly between targets sent at a lower rate.
  • The order: rti_connect(), rti_claim(), stream, rti_release(), rti_disconnect().
Command What it does Runs RTIClient Real-time streaming control of one robot, beside its RobotClient. In the client (a class) rti_connect Pair this PC with the robot and switch to a real-time mode. At once rti_claim Claim real-time control: the robot starts applying your commands. At once rti_release End the real-time stream: brake to rest and hold, still paired. At once rti_disconnect Unpair the PC and switch the robot to IDLE mode. At once rti_set_start_pose_check Switch the check of the first command after a claim on or off. At once rti_set_rate_limiter Switch the real-time rate limiter on or off. At once rti_set_tcp_vel_limit Cap the tool's straight-line speed under real-time control. At once rti_set_vel_scale Scale the real-time joint speed limits down. At once rti_set_command_timeout Set how long the robot waits for the next real-time command. At once rti_set_gravity_comp Switch gravity compensation on or off for real-time control. At once rti_set_dynamics_ff Choose the inertia and Coriolis feedforward of real-time streams. At once rti_set_servo_generator Choose how the robot fills in the ticks between position targets. At once rti_set_min_duration Make each planned move last at least a multiple of your interval. At once rti_set_pace Cap the generator's speed at a multiple of your target's speed. At once rti_set_lowpass Filter incoming real-time commands with a low-pass filter. At once rti_set_state_rate Set how often the robot sends its state packet in SOFT_RTI. At once

docs.title: Robot control commands
docs.text:
The commands that switch the motors on and off, home the arm, change the robot's mode, stop or pause a program, and decide which client controls the robot.

All robot control commands:

  • Run at once. They are not queued. The robot acts on each one when it arrives, also while moves are queued.
  • Can wait for the robot. With wait=True, or on a client created with RobotClient(sync=True), a call waits until the robot's status shows the change: up to 10 s, or 3 minutes for home(). Without a wait, the call returns once the robot has answered.
  • Mostly take control. A command that changes what the robot does claims control for its client when no client holds it. Each page says whether its command takes control or is open to every client.
Command What it does Runs enable Enable the robot, so that it can home and move. At once disable Disable the robot: it stops at once and holds every joint still. At once home Home the arm: find each joint's reference position. At once clear_errors Clear the latched errors, and the abort after a failed move. At once enter_idle_mode Switch to IDLE mode. At once enter_exec_mode Switch to EXEC mode, where the robot runs queued moves. At once enter_jog_mode Switch to JOG mode, where jog() moves one joint at a time. At once stop Stop the robot's motion and cancel every queued move. At once pause Pause the running program: brake along its path and hold. At once resume Resume a paused program from where it stopped. At once safety_stop Switch the motors off: the arm goes limp and falls. At once release_safety_stop Switch the motors back on after a safety stop. At once enter_flashing_mode Hand the CAN bus to a firmware flasher; the motors let go. At once exit_flashing_mode End firmware flashing and take the CAN bus back. At once take_control Take control of the robot for this client. At once release_control Give up control of the robot. At once control_holder Return the client that holds control, or None. In the client holds_control Return whether this client holds control. In the client set_force_confirm Require a button press at the robot for a forced takeover. At once

docs.title: Safety and dynamics commands
docs.text:
The switches for the robot's model-based torques (gravity compensation, the inertia, Coriolis and friction feedforwards, friction compensation in freedrive), collision detection, the declared payload, the safety zones and the walls at the joint limits in freedrive.

  • They apply to the whole robot, for every client, until changed or until the robot software restarts.
  • Some switch a protection off. Their pages say so in a warning.
Command What it does Runs set_gravity_comp Switch gravity compensation on or off for the whole robot. At once set_inertia_comp Switch the inertia feedforward on or off for the whole robot. At once set_coriolis_comp Switch the Coriolis feedforward on or off for the whole robot. At once set_friction_ff Switch the friction feedforward on or off for the whole robot. At once set_friction_comp Switch friction compensation in freedrive on or off. At once set_payload Declare the part the gripper holds: its mass and centre of mass. At once set_collision_detection Set how the robot reacts when the arm hits something. At once get_zones Return the safety zones in force. At once reload_zones Re-read the safety zones from their files and apply them. At once get_joint_walls Return the freedrive joint walls in force, with their stable ranges. At once set_joint_wall Change one joint's freedrive wall, live. At once save_joint_walls Save the live freedrive walls into the robot XML. At once

docs.title: Status and data commands
docs.text:
The commands that read the robot: joint angles, the tool's pose, its status, latched errors, the health of every part, its hardware and versions, and whether a pose can be reached.

  • The get_ commands ask the robot and wait for its answer.
  • latest_status() and errors() ask nothing: they read the status the robot last sent. Every field is in the Status fields reference.
Command What it does Runs get_joints Return the measured joint angles, in degrees. At once get_pose Return the measured pose of the tool centre point. At once latest_status Return the latest status the robot sent, without asking it. In the client get_status Ask the robot for its state now, with the joint angles. At once errors Return the errors and warnings latched on the robot. In the client is_reachable Check whether the arm can reach a pose, without moving it. At once get_health Return the robot's health summary, one level per part. At once get_hardware Return what the drives, the CAN bus and the control box report. At once get_versions Return the version of every part of the robot. At once

docs.title: Waiting commands
docs.text:
The calls that wait, in your program, for something the robot reports: the queued moves to finish, a mode, homing, the robot enabled, the errors cleared, or any condition of your own.

All of them:

  • Run in the client. They read the status the robot sends, or the answers to the commands this client sent. A wait sends nothing to the robot.
  • End with an exception when time runs out. A wait that runs out of time raises RobotTimeout; so does a wait during which the connection drops.
Command What it does Runs wait_idle Wait until every command this client queued has finished. In the client wait_motion_complete Wait until the last command this client queued has finished. In the client wait_mode Wait until the robot is in a given mode. In the client wait_homed Wait until the robot is homed and no homing is running. In the client wait_enabled Wait until the robot is enabled. In the client wait_error_reset Wait until the robot reports no error and no warning. In the client wait Wait until the robot's status meets a condition of your own. In the client

docs.title: Error and event codes
docs.text:
Every error, warning and event the robot reports has a number and a name, for example 2103 WATCHDOG. A joint's code carries the joint in front of it, for example J3:WATCHDOG. The dashboard, the activity log, the Python client's exceptions and the status messages all show the same number and name, so a code from any of them can be looked up here.

This page is generated from the runtime's error catalog at the release this documentation describes.

Every code has a number, a name and a kind. Kinds: stop: the robot stops and is disabled; fails: the command, move or program fails or is refused; the robot is not affected; warning: the robot keeps running; event: information only.

docs.title: 1xxx: Safety: E-stop, limits, walls, speed, zones, self-collision, collisions
1001 ESTOP
docs.text:
Emergency stop pressed. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: An emergency stop button is pressed, or its circuit is open.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Make the area safe and release the E-stop. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 1002 SW_ESTOP
docs.text:
Software emergency stop active. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: A software emergency stop was set by a command or the dashboard.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Release the software E-stop. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 1101 OUT_OF_RANGE
docs.text:
Joint outside its software limit. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The joint's measured position went past its software limit while the robot moved it. A collision, a push or a move the limits should have stopped can cause this.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared. Afterwards only motion back toward the allowed range is possible. In IDLE freedrive this is only a warning.
  • Fix: Clear errors, then jog the joint back inside its range. Find what moved it out.

docs.title: 1102 SOFT_LIMIT_WARNING
docs.text:
Joint past its software limit. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The joint is past its software limit: it was moved there by hand in freedrive, or it rests there.
  • Effect: Warning only. Jog, EXEC and RTI motion may only move the joint back inside.
  • Fix: Move the joint back inside its limit. The warning then clears itself.

docs.title: 1103 HARD_LIMIT
docs.text:
Joint past its hard limit. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: A joint without an endstop or freedrive wall passed its hard limit, where its cables start to wind up. Nothing physical stops it there.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared. Afterwards only motion back toward the allowed range is possible.
  • Fix: Check the joint's cables. Clear errors, then move the joint back inside.

docs.title: 1104 BEYOND_ENDSTOP
docs.text:
Joint position beyond its endstop. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The measured position is further past the joint's physical endstop than the robot XML allows (<endstop_tolerance_deg>). A real arm cannot be there, so the position reference is wrong: a slipped belt or gear, or an encoder fault.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared. Homing is invalidated.
  • Fix: Check the joint's belt, gears and encoder. Clear errors, then home the robot again.

docs.title: 1105 JOINT_WALL
docs.text:
Joint pushed through its freedrive wall. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The joint was pushed through its freedrive wall by more than the wall's breakthrough distance, and this wall is set to stop (robot XML <freedrive_wall freedrive="stop">).
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared. Afterwards only motion back toward the allowed range is possible.
  • Fix: Clear errors and enable the robot, then move the joint back inside the wall.

docs.title: 1106 JOINT_WALL_WARNING
docs.text:
Joint pushed through its freedrive wall. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The joint was pushed through its freedrive wall in freedrive by more than the wall's breakthrough distance.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: Turn the joint back inside the wall. On J6 check the cables too: its wall marks the cable wind-up limit.

docs.title: 1201 OVERSPEED
docs.text:
Joint too fast. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The joint's filtered speed stayed above its velocity limit times the safety margin.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Find what commanded the joint so fast. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 1202 OVERSPEED_WARNING
docs.text:
Joint too fast. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The joint's filtered speed went above its velocity limit times the safety margin. The check runs in warn-only mode.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: If this was normal motion, raise the joint's limit or margin before the check is set to stop. RTI.log has the peak.

docs.title: 1203 TCP_OVERSPEED
docs.text:
Tool too fast. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The tool moved faster than <max_tcp_velocity> times the safety margin.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Find what commanded the arm so fast. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 1204 TCP_OVERSPEED_WARNING
docs.text:
Tool too fast. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The tool moved faster than <max_tcp_velocity> times the safety margin. The check runs in warn-only mode.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: If this was normal motion, raise <max_tcp_velocity> or its margin. RTI.log has the peak.

docs.title: 1205 TRACKING
docs.text:
Joint lagging its command. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: During EXEC motion the joint fell too far behind its commanded position: a bump, a collision or a stall.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check for an obstruction or an overload. Clear errors, then continue.

docs.title: 1206 TRACKING_WARNING
docs.text:
Joint lagging its command. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: During EXEC motion the joint fell further behind its commanded position than its limit. The check runs in warn-only mode.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: If this was normal motion, raise <tracking_limit_deg> for the joint before the check is set to stop.

docs.title: 1301 ZONE_VIOLATION
docs.text:
Safety zone violated. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The tool or a tool sphere left an allowed zone or entered a forbidden zone of the active cell. The message names the zone.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared. Afterwards only motion that does not go deeper into the zone is possible.
  • Fix: Clear errors, then move the robot out of the zone. If the zone is wrong, correct it in config/cells.

docs.title: 1302 ZONE_WARNING
docs.text:
Robot in a warning zone. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The robot is inside a warning zone of the active cell.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears when the robot leaves the zone.
  • Fix: None needed.

docs.title: 1401 SELF_COLLISION
docs.text:
Self-collision. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: Two parts of the arm came closer than the self-collision margin on the measured pose. The message names the pair.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared. Afterwards only directions that open the gap are possible.
  • Fix: Clear errors, then jog the two parts apart. If a planned move caused it, report the pair and the move.

docs.title: 1402 SELF_COLLISION_WARNING
docs.text:
Self-collision margin reached. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: Two parts of the arm are closer than the self-collision margin. The check runs in warn-only mode.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: None needed. Once the check is trusted, set <self_collision><reaction> to stop.

docs.title: 1403 SELF_COLLISION_STALE
docs.text:
Self-collision check not running. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The self-collision worker has not reported for half a second, so self-collisions are not being watched.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running without its self-collision check.
  • Fix: Check the self-collision log in the Logs tab. The worker restarts with the service.

docs.title: 1501 COLLISION
docs.text:
Collision detected. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: While the robot moved the joint, the external torque on it rose above its collision threshold (robot XML <collision_torque_nm>) compared with the torque it had at rest before the move: the arm hit something, or carries a load it was not told about.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check what the arm hit and clear the way. Declare a held part with set_payload. Clear errors, then continue. A program that pushes on purpose switches the check off with set_collision_detection.

docs.title: 1502 COLLISION_WARNING
docs.text:
Collision detected. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: While the robot moved the joint, the external torque on it rose above its collision threshold compared with the torque it had at rest before the move. The check runs in warn-only mode.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: If nothing was hit, raise <collision_torque_nm> for the joint or re-measure it with api_tests/76 before the check is set to stop. RTI.log has the peak.

docs.title: 1503 CONTACT_WARNING
docs.text:
Contact detected. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: While the robot moved the joint, the external torque on it rose above its contact threshold (robot XML <contact_torque_nm>) compared with the torque it had at rest before the move.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: None needed if the contact was expected. If nothing touched the arm, raise <contact_torque_nm> for the joint or re-measure it with api_tests/76.

docs.title: 2101 TEMPERATURE
docs.text:
Motor overheating. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive reports that the joint's motor is too hot.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Let the motor cool down and check the joint for a high load. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2102 VBUS
docs.text:
Drive supply voltage out of range. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the joint reports its supply voltage outside its range.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the power supply and the joint's power wiring. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2103 WATCHDOG
docs.text:
Drive watchdog tripped. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the joint received no command within its watchdog time: the CAN link to it, or RTI's loop, stalled.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the joint's CAN cable and power. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2104 ENCODER
docs.text:
Encoder fault. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the joint reports a lost or corrupted encoder signal.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the joint's encoder cable and connector. Clear errors, then home the robot again.

docs.title: 2105 DRIVER
docs.text:
Drive fault. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the joint reports an internal hardware fault.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Switch the robot off and on. If the fault returns, replace the drive.

docs.title: 2106 VELOCITY
docs.text:
Motor over its velocity limit. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive reports that the joint's motor exceeded its velocity limit.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check for a collision or an obstruction. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2107 CURRENT
docs.text:
Motor overcurrent. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the joint detected an overcurrent.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the joint for a mechanical jam. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2108 ESTOP_MOTOR
docs.text:
Drive emergency stop input. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the joint reports an emergency stop on its own input.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the drive's E-stop input wiring. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2109 HOLD_OSCILLATION_WARNING
docs.text:
Joint buzzing while holding. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The motor current keeps swinging fast while the joint is commanded to stand still: the drive's control loop is fighting itself, which you hear as a buzz.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: Lower the joint's speed gains (KPV, KPP). If that does not help, check the encoder magnet and the mechanics.

docs.title: 2201 GRIPPER_MOTOR_TEMPERATURE
docs.text:
Gripper motor overheating. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive reports that the gripper motor is too hot.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Let the gripper motor cool down. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2202 GRIPPER_MOTOR_VBUS
docs.text:
Gripper supply voltage out of range. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the gripper reports its supply voltage outside its range.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the power supply and the gripper's power wiring. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2203 GRIPPER_MOTOR_WATCHDOG
docs.text:
Gripper watchdog tripped. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the gripper received no command within its watchdog time.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the gripper's CAN cable and power. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2204 GRIPPER_MOTOR_ENCODER
docs.text:
Gripper encoder fault. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the gripper reports a lost or corrupted encoder signal.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the gripper's encoder cable and connector. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2205 GRIPPER_MOTOR_DRIVER
docs.text:
Gripper drive fault. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the gripper reports an internal hardware fault.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Switch the robot off and on. If the fault returns, replace the gripper drive.

docs.title: 2206 GRIPPER_MOTOR_VELOCITY
docs.text:
Gripper motor over its velocity limit. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive reports that the gripper motor exceeded its velocity limit.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the gripper for an obstruction. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2207 GRIPPER_MOTOR_CURRENT
docs.text:
Gripper motor overcurrent. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the gripper detected an overcurrent.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the gripper for a mechanical jam. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2208 GRIPPER_MOTOR_ESTOP
docs.text:
Gripper drive emergency stop input. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The drive of the gripper reports an emergency stop on its own input.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the gripper drive's E-stop input wiring. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2301 GRIPPER_ERROR
docs.text:
Gripper fault. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The gripper reports a general fault.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Clear errors and enable the robot. If the fault returns, switch the gripper off and on.

docs.title: 2302 GRIPPER_ESTOP
docs.text:
Gripper emergency stop. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The gripper reports an emergency stop signal.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Clear the gripper's E-stop condition. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2303 GRIPPER_TIMEOUT
docs.text:
Gripper timeout. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The gripper reports a timeout: it got no command in time.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the gripper's CAN cable and power. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 2304 GRIPPER_SETTLE_TIMEOUT
docs.text:
Gripper did not settle. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A gripper command did not report a settled position within 5 s.
  • Effect: The gripper command fails. The rest of the program continues.
  • Fix: Check that the jaws move freely and the gripper is powered.

docs.title: 3001 CAN_LOST
docs.text:
Drive connection lost. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: No CAN data arrived from the joint's drive for too long.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared. Homing is invalidated.
  • Fix: Check the CAN cable, its termination and the joint's power. Clear errors, then home the robot again.

docs.title: 3002 CAN_STALE
docs.text:
Drive data late. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The joint's CAN data is getting old: its drive answers late.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: None needed if it clears. If it repeats, check the CAN cable and the bus load.

docs.title: 3003 CAN_REPLY_MISSED_WARNING
docs.text:
Drive replies keep arriving late. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The joint's drive replies missed RTI's CAN read 5 or more times a second for 3 s, so its measured state was one tick old on those ticks.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: Check that RTI's start-up line about the CAN interrupt threads reports no problem. RTI.log has the peak.

docs.title: 3004 GRIPPER_DISCONNECTED
docs.text:
Gripper connection lost. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The gripper sends no CAN replies.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared. Homing is invalidated.
  • Fix: Check the gripper's CAN cable and power. Clear errors, then home the robot again.

docs.title: 3101 EXEC_LINK_LOST
docs.text:
Executor stopped responding. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The command executor went silent while the robot ran EXEC motion.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Restart the service. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.title: 3102 RTI_LINK_LOST
docs.text:
External PC stopped sending. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The PC that held RTI control stopped sending setpoints.
  • Effect: The robot braked to rest within its limits and refused the stream. It is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the network and the PC's program. Clear errors, then claim control again.

docs.title: 3201 SEND_TIMEOUT
docs.text:
Trajectory not taken by RTI. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The executor could not hand a trajectory to RTI in time: RTI is not taking trajectory batches.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check in the Logs tab that RTI is running. Restart the service if it is not.

docs.title: 4001 NOT_HOMED
docs.text:
Robot not homed. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The robot has not been homed since RTI started, so the joint positions have no reference.
  • Effect: Warning only. Motion that needs a reference (EXEC, RTI) is refused until the robot is homed.
  • Fix: Home the robot.

docs.title: 4002 HOMING_FAILED
docs.text:
Joint homing failed. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: Homing of this joint failed. The message says why: an endstop or Hall sensor not reached in time, two passes too far apart, no position at the endstop, or the joint homed away from where this arm always homes.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Move the arm to its park pose by hand and check that nothing is in the way. Clear errors, enable and home again. After a deliberate mechanical change, accept the new reference in System Info, Arms (homing).

docs.title: 4003 GRIPPER_HOMING_FAILED
docs.text:
Gripper homing failed. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The gripper's calibration did not finish in time, or its motor homing found no endstop. The message says which.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check that the jaws move freely and the gripper is powered. Clear errors, enable and home again.

docs.title: 4004 HOMING_ABORTED
docs.text:
Homing aborted. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: An error latched while the robot was homing, or the homing was interrupted before it finished (Stop, Disable or another mode).
  • Effect: Homing stopped and the robot is not homed.
  • Fix: Clear any error the error list names, then home the robot again.

docs.title: 4005 HOMING_INVALIDATED
docs.text:
Homing invalidated. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The position reference can no longer be trusted: a drive lost its connection, a joint measured past its endstop, or firmware was flashed. The message says which.
  • Effect: The robot is not homed. Motion that needs a reference is refused.
  • Fix: Home the robot again.

docs.title: 4006 HALL_CHECK_REFUSED
docs.text:
Hall sensor check refused. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The Hall sensor check cannot start now. The message says why.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Do what the message asks, usually going to IDLE, then start the check again.

docs.title: 4007 FREE_JOINT_REFUSED
docs.text:
Freeing a joint refused. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A joint cannot be freed for hand turning now. The message says why.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Do what the message asks, usually going to IDLE, then try again.

docs.title: 4008 JOINT_TEST_REFUSED
docs.text:
Joint test move refused. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A test move cannot start now. The message says why.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Do what the message asks, usually enabling the arm in IDLE, then try again.

docs.title: 5001 PLAN_FAIL
docs.text:
Trajectory planning failed. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The planner could not plan the move. The message gives the reason.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the move's target and options. The executor's log in the Logs tab has the detail.

docs.title: 5002 MOTION_ABORTED
docs.text:
Program aborted. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A queued command failed or motion was interrupted, so the rest of the program was cancelled. The message names the command and the reason.
  • Effect: New motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Fix what the failing command's error says. Clear errors, then send the program again.

docs.title: 5003 ABORTED
docs.text:
Command cancelled. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The command was cancelled before it ran, because an earlier command failed or motion was interrupted.
  • Effect: The command did not run.
  • Fix: Clear errors, then send the program again.

docs.title: 5004 STOPPED
docs.text:
Command stopped. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A stop ended the program before this command ran.
  • Effect: The command did not run.
  • Fix: Send the command again if it is still needed.

docs.title: 5005 SETTLE_TIMEOUT
docs.text:
Move did not settle. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The final position did not settle within tolerance in time. The strict completion policy reports this as a failure.
  • Effect: The command fails. The rest of the program continues.
  • Fix: Check for a load or an obstruction near the target, or use the settled completion policy.

docs.title: 5006 JOINT_LIMIT
docs.text:
Move outside the joint limits. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The planned move would take a joint outside its software limits. The message names the joint and its limits.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Change the target, or move the arm back inside its limits first.

docs.title: 5007 ZONE_LIMIT
docs.text:
Move into a safety zone. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The planned move would take the tool or a robot sphere into a stop zone of the active cell.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Change the target or the path so that it stays out of the zone. If the zone is wrong, correct it in config/cells.

docs.title: 5008 ZONE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE
docs.text:
Zone check unavailable. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: Safety zones are active, but the planner has no robot model to check them.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Find in the executor's log (Logs tab) why the robot model did not load, then restart the service.

docs.title: 5009 ACCEL_LIMIT_VIOLATION
docs.text:
Planned acceleration over its limit. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The planned trajectory's acceleration exceeds the limit it was planned against. This is an internal planner check.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Lower the move's speed or acceleration, or use another profile. Report it if it repeats.

docs.title: 5010 DURATION_INFEASIBLE
docs.text:
Requested duration too short. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The move cannot be done in the requested duration within the limits.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Ask for a longer duration (the message gives the shortest possible), or leave the duration out.

docs.title: 5011 INVALID_DURATION
docs.text:
Invalid duration. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The requested duration is not a positive number.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Give a duration above 0 s, or leave it out.

docs.title: 5012 STOP_FALLBACK
docs.text:
Stop not confirmed. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: RTI did not confirm a controlled stop within 1.5 s. RTI may run older code than the executor.
  • Effect: The robot was switched to IDLE instead.
  • Fix: Restart the service so that RTI and the executor run the same code. If it repeats, check RTI.log in the Logs tab.

docs.title: 5101 IK_TARGET_UNREACHABLE
docs.text:
Target out of reach. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: No joint solution reaches the requested pose: it is outside the arm's workspace or joint limits.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Choose a pose within reach, or approach it from another configuration.

docs.title: 5102 IK_PARTIAL_PATH
docs.text:
Path only partly reachable. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The inverse kinematics could solve only part of the Cartesian path.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Shorten the path, or move it closer to the arm's reachable region.

docs.title: 5103 IK_MARGIN_VIOLATION
docs.text:
Path too close to a limit. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The solved path passes too close to a joint limit or a singularity.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Adjust the target pose, or plan the path through another region.

docs.title: 5104 IK_POSE_ERROR
docs.text:
Solution misses the pose. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The solved joint configuration does not reach the requested pose within tolerance, often near a singularity.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Move the target away from singular poses, or use a joint move.

docs.title: 5105 IK_BRANCH_JUMP
docs.text:
Configuration flip on the path. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: Along the Cartesian path the solution jumped to another arm configuration, so a joint would flip.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Shorten the path, start from another pose, or use a joint move.

docs.title: 5106 IK_SINGULARITY_WARNING
docs.text:
Path near a singularity. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The planned path passes near a kinematic singularity.
  • Effect: Warning only: the move runs.
  • Fix: If the motion is rough, plan the path away from the singularity.

docs.title: 5107 CARTESIAN_PATH_DEVIATION
docs.text:
Tool strays from the path. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The planned tool path strays from the programmed line or curve by more than the tolerance.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Move the path away from singular poses, shorten it, or use a joint move.

docs.title: 5108 CURVE_BLEND_UNSUPPORTED
docs.text:
Blending not supported on curves. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: Curve commands cannot be blended yet.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Send the curve with blend set to 0.

docs.title: 5109 CURVE_GEOMETRY_INVALID
docs.text:
Invalid curve. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The curve's points do not define a valid curve, for example collinear points for an arc.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the curve's points against the command reference.

docs.title: 5110 BAD_ARGUMENTS
docs.text:
Invalid curve arguments. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A curve command has the wrong number of values or an unknown frame.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the command's arguments against the command reference.

docs.title: 5201 TOPPRA_UNAVAILABLE
docs.text:
TOPPRA profile unavailable. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The TOPPRA profile was requested, but its package cannot be imported.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Install the toppra package, or choose another profile.

docs.title: 5202 TOPPRA_INFEASIBLE
docs.text:
TOPPRA found no solution. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: TOPPRA could not time the path within the limits.
  • Effect: The move does not start. The rest of the program is cancelled, and motion commands are refused until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the speed and acceleration limits, or choose another profile.

docs.title: 5301 LIMIT_REACHED
docs.text:
Jog stopped at a limit. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: The jog reached a joint limit or a workspace limit.
  • Effect: The jog stops there. Jogging away from the limit is possible.
  • Fix: Jog the other way.

docs.title: 5302 SELF_COLLISION_BLOCK
docs.text:
Jog stopped at the collision margin. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: Jogging further would bring two parts of the arm too close.
  • Effect: The jog stops there.
  • Fix: Jog the other way, or move another joint.

docs.title: 6001 UNKNOWN_CMD
docs.text:
Unknown command. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The command name is not known.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Check the spelling against the command reference.

docs.title: 6002 BAD_JSON
docs.text:
Invalid message. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The message is not valid JSON.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Check how the client encodes its messages.

docs.title: 6003 BAD_ARGS
docs.text:
Invalid arguments. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The command's arguments failed validation. The message says which.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Check the number and types of the arguments against the command reference.

docs.title: 6004 BAD_OPTIONS
docs.text:
Invalid motion options. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The command's motion options failed validation.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Check the profile, speed, blend and completion policy values.

docs.title: 6005 BAD_PROFILE
docs.text:
Unknown motion profile. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The requested trajectory profile is not known.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Use a profile from the command reference.

docs.title: 6006 BAD_IK_SOLVER
docs.text:
Unknown IK solver. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The requested IK solver is not known.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Use a solver from the command reference.

docs.title: 6007 BAD_POLICY
docs.text:
Unknown completion policy. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The requested completion policy is not known.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Use commanded, settled or strict.

docs.title: 6008 BAD_PIN
docs.text:
Invalid I/O pin. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The command names an I/O pin the robot does not have.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Use a pin number in the range the message gives.

docs.title: 6009 FORBIDDEN
docs.text:
Connection not allowed. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The client's IP address is not on the executor's allowed list.
  • Effect: The connection is closed.
  • Fix: Connect from an allowed machine, or add its address to RCB_ALLOWED_IPS.

docs.title: 6010 REJECTED
docs.text:
Command not allowed now. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The command is not allowed in the robot's current mode or state. The message says what it needs.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Bring the robot into the mode or state the message names, then send the command again.

docs.title: 6011 QUEUE_FULL
docs.text:
Motion queue full. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The motion queue holds its maximum number of commands.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Wait until queued moves finish, then send the command again.

docs.title: 6012 UNHANDLED
docs.text:
Command not handled. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The executor accepted the command but has no handler for it. This is an internal error.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Report it with the command and the executor's log.

docs.title: 6013 INTERNAL
docs.text:
Internal error. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The command failed with an unexpected error.
  • Effect: The command did not complete.
  • Fix: Report it with the executor's log from the Logs tab.

docs.title: 6014 MODE_REJECTED
docs.text:
Mode change refused. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: RTI refused the mode change. The message says why: not homed, not enabled, an active error, or a change that is not allowed from this mode.
  • Effect: The robot stays in its mode.
  • Fix: Do what the message asks first, then request the mode again.

docs.title: 6015 ENABLE_REJECTED
docs.text:
Enable refused. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: RTI refused to enable the robot. The message says why, for example an active error or a safety stop.
  • Effect: The robot stays disabled.
  • Fix: Clear the errors or the safety condition first, then enable the robot again.

docs.title: 6016 PAYLOAD_LIMIT
docs.text:
Payload not accepted. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The payload is above the robot's maximum, or its values are not valid.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Check the mass and the centre of mass against <max_payload_kg> in the robot XML.

docs.title: 6017 WALL_OFF
docs.text:
No freedrive wall on this joint. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: This joint has no freedrive wall to change: joint walls are off, or there is no inertia for it.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Turn joint walls on in <haptic_walls>, or choose another joint.

docs.title: 6018 WALL_UNSTABLE
docs.text:
Wall setting unstable. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The requested wall frequency and damping would be unstable at this filter setting.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Use a frequency and damping ratio inside the range the message gives.

docs.title: 6019 NO_ROBOT_MODEL
docs.text:
No robot model. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The executor has no robot model, so it cannot check reachability.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Find in the executor's log (Logs tab) why the model did not load, then restart the service.

docs.title: 6020 SUPERSEDED
docs.text:
Gripper command replaced. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A newer gripper command replaced this one before it settled.
  • Effect: This command ends and the newer one runs.
  • Fix: None needed.

docs.title: 6021 CAPTURE_REFUSED
docs.text:
Capture not started. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A telemetry capture cannot start or stop: one is already running, the length is outside 1 to 60 s, the recorder process is not running, nothing was captured, or a stop was asked while none runs. The message says which.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Wait for the running capture to finish, ask for a length of 1 to 60 s, or check that the recorder runs.

docs.title: 6022 CLIENT_TOO_OLD
docs.text:
Client too old for pose commands. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The client declares no command protocol version, so it may be from before 0.9.0, when pose angles had another meaning. A pose it sends could turn the tool to another orientation.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Use the robotclient that came with the robot's runtime. A client that sends raw JSON adds "protocol": 2 to each message.

docs.title: 6023 NO_GRIPPER
docs.text:
No gripper. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The robot has no CAN gripper, so a gripper command cannot run.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Leave gripper commands out of the program, or select a CAN gripper as <active_gripper> in config/system.xml and restart the robot service.

docs.title: 6024 GRIPPER_MOTOR_MODE
docs.text:
Gripper in motor mode. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The gripper is in motor mode, where the robot sends it no target, so a gripper move cannot run.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Switch it to firmware mode with set_gripper_ctrl_mode(2), then send the command again.

docs.title: 6025 RTI_NOT_RUNNING
docs.text:
Measured values unavailable. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: RTI is not running, or the robot is in flashing mode, so the measured values in the robot's memory are old.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Check the robot service and RTI.log (Logs tab), or leave flashing mode, then ask again.

docs.title: 6101 CONTROL_HELD
docs.text:
Control held by another client. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: Another client holds control of the robot.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Release control on that client, or take control. A forced takeover asks for confirmation at the control box.

docs.title: 6102 CONFIRM_REQUIRED
docs.text:
Takeover not confirmed. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: A forced takeover needs a confirmation at the control box, and it was denied or timed out.
  • Effect: Control stays with the other client.
  • Fix: Try again and confirm at the control box, or ask the other client to release control.

docs.title: 6103 CONFIRM_BUSY
docs.text:
Takeover already waiting. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: Another forced takeover is already waiting for confirmation at the control box.
  • Effect: The command is refused. Nothing changes.
  • Fix: Answer or wait out that request, then try again.

docs.title: 6201 RTI_POSITION_LIMIT
docs.text:
PC target outside the joint limits. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The PC's RTI target would move the joint past its software limit, or toward it faster than the joint can still stop.
  • Effect: The robot braked to rest within its limits and refused the stream. It is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Keep the PC's targets inside the joint limits and slow down before them. Clear errors, then claim control again.

docs.title: 6202 RTI_VELOCITY_LIMIT
docs.text:
PC stream too fast. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The PC's hard-RTI stream moved the joint faster than its RTI velocity limit plus 10 %.
  • Effect: The robot braked to rest within its limits and refused the stream. It is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Slow the PC's trajectory down to the joint's velocity limit. Clear errors, then claim control again.

docs.title: 6203 RTI_ACCELERATION_LIMIT
docs.text:
PC stream accelerates too hard. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The PC's hard-RTI stream changed the joint's speed faster than its acceleration limit plus 10 %: a jump, a sudden stop or a wild packet.
  • Effect: The robot braked to rest within its limits and refused the stream. It is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Send a smooth trajectory, or filter noisy targets (rti_set_lowpass). Clear errors, then claim control again.

docs.title: 6204 RTI_JERK_LIMIT
docs.text:
PC stream too jerky. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The PC's hard-RTI stream changed the joint's acceleration faster than its jerk limit plus 10 %.
  • Effect: The robot braked to rest within its limits and refused the stream. It is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Send a jerk-limited trajectory, or filter noisy targets (rti_set_lowpass). Clear errors, then claim control again.

docs.title: 6205 RTI_NO_SEND_TIME
docs.text:
PC packet without its send time. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: A hard-RTI position command arrived without the PC's send time. Hard RTI follows the PC's own timing and needs it.
  • Effect: The robot braked to rest within its limits and refused the stream. It is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Keep send times on in the client (the default), or use SOFT_RTI for a sender without them. Clear errors, then claim control again.

docs.title: 6206 RTI_START_POSE
docs.text:
First setpoint too far from the arm. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: The first command of an RTI session is too far from where the arm is. The start-pose check refuses a session that would begin with a jump.
  • Effect: The robot braked to rest within its limits and refused the stream. It is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Start the stream from the arm's measured position (the state packets give it). Clear errors, then claim control again.

docs.title: 7001 ZONE_CONFIG
docs.text:
Cell file unreadable. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The safety-zone cell file could not be read.
  • Effect: The zones in force stay unchanged.
  • Fix: Fix the cell file the message names, or empty <active_cell>, then reload the zones.

docs.title: 7002 FILTER_CONFIG
docs.text:
Filter file invalid. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The filter file config/filters.xml could not be parsed.
  • Effect: The filters in force stay unchanged.
  • Fix: Fix config/filters.xml where the message says, then reload the filters.

docs.title: 7003 RECIPE_DIR
docs.text:
Recipe folder unreadable. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The telemetry recipe folder could not be read.
  • Effect: The recipes in force stay unchanged.
  • Fix: Check that data_recipe exists and is readable, then reload the recipes.

docs.title: 7004 SELF_COLLISION_MODEL
docs.text:
Self-collision model not built. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: Self-collision checking is on, but its model could not be built from the geometry files.
  • Effect: Reachability checks are refused.
  • Fix: Fix the geometry files the message names (robot or gripper XML), then restart the service.

docs.title: 7005 SAVE_FAILED
docs.text:
Walls not saved. Kind: fails.

  • Cause: The freedrive walls could not be written to the robot XML.
  • Effect: The file is unchanged. The walls in force stay as they are.
  • Fix: Check that the robot XML is writable and valid, then save again.

docs.title: 8001 LOOP_DEGRADED
docs.text:
Control loop running slow. Kind: warning.

  • Cause: RTI's control loop runs slower than its configured rate.
  • Effect: Warning only: the robot keeps running. The warning clears itself when the condition ends.
  • Fix: Check the CPU load and temperature, and whether a drive went silent. Heavy jobs on the Pi slow the loop.

docs.title: 8002 LOOP_CRITICAL
docs.text:
Control loop critically slow. Kind: stop.

  • Cause: RTI's control loop was critically slow: its period stayed over 1.5 times nominal for a second, or one tick took over 3 times nominal.
  • Effect: The robot stops and is disabled until errors are cleared.
  • Fix: Check the CPU load and temperature, and the timing in the RT Diagnostics tab. Clear errors, then enable the robot.

docs.text: Mode changed. Kind: event.

docs.title: 9002 STATE_CHANGE

docs.title: 9004 CMD_STARTED

docs.title: 9005 CMD_COMPLETED

docs.title: 9006 CMD_EXECUTED

docs.title: 9007 JOG_STARTED

docs.title: 9008 JOG_STOPPED

docs.title: 9009 LIMIT_CLEARED

docs.title: 9010 COMPENSATION_CHANGED

docs.title: 9011 PAYLOAD_CHANGED

docs.title: 9012 HOMING_STARTED

docs.title: 9013 HOMING_JOINT_HOMED

docs.title: 9014 HOMING_COMPLETED

docs.title: 9015 HALL_CHECK

docs.title: 9016 BLEND_SPLICED

docs.title: 9017 BLEND_SPLICE_REJECTED
